target_customer: Venture-backed startups in AI, SaaS, defense, fintech and space that need D&O, cyber and tech E&O coverage to close enterprise deals
problem: Startups struggle to get vendor-ready insurance quickly, and carriers lack models for emerging risks like AI liability. RiskCube brokers coverage and plans to build its own risk models.
business_model: insurance brokerage commissions, with planned proprietary risk models and new insurance products

founders.name: Andrei Craciunescu
prior_employers: WTW (Willis Towers Watson), risk and analytics
education: PhD-level research in financial mathematics, Technical University of Munich
founders.background_notes: Licensed insurance broker per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Brokerage tooling is standard software, but modeling risks with little claims data using stochastic simulation is harder; the CEO has a quantitative risk background.

defensibility.rationale: A broker license is required, which is a modest barrier. Digital startup brokers such as Vouch and Embroker already served the segment and quotes can be compared by customers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Newfront was agreed to be acquired by WTW in December 2025 per trade press; no action against RiskCube found. Many AI insurance brokers raised large rounds in 2026.

market_need_then: The CEO says startups struggled to get coverage while he worked at WTW, and enterprise buyers require proof of insurance. The company reports a case where a D&O premium fell from 11,000 to 4,400 USD (company claim).

branding.domain_note: riskcube.com, exact match per YC listing; acquisition history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, focused on speed and simplicity

brand_strength.rationale: Only founder profile pieces found; name resembles CyberCube, an unrelated insurance analytics firm.

outcome_analysis: RiskCube is a one-founder brokerage from Fall 2024 led by a former WTW and Munich Re risk analyst. It sells coverage to YC-backed startups and plans proprietary risk models, but no priced round is verified and it competes with funded digital brokers. The outcome is undetermined.
notes: Funding: VCBacked and Coverager list about 500K pre-seed (Dec 2024) from YC, aggregator only, unverified so not recorded as a round. The competitor search returned vendor pages dated 2025 to 2026, nothing dated near the batch, so the list is empty although Vouch, Embroker and Newfront are known peers. The Science Times claim about licenses in California and Delaware is from one outlet. Completeness pass: the $500K pre-seed (2024-12, Y Combinator) is recorded from VCBacked alone (Coverager agrees per earlier notes); no primary announcement found, and it may be the YC standard deal.
